title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-20
content:
Summary:
Investigating a throughput regression observed after the 2026-02-18 rollout of the continuous-batching defaults change. Production p50 token throughput dropped ~18% for large-sequence workloads (>1024). p95 latency increased and we saw increased tail on some worker pods (GPU utilization lower than expected).

Timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2026-02-18 03:00 UTC: Feature flag `continuous_batching.default_enabled=true` rolled to 100% for hosted api.
- 2026-02-19 06:20 UTC: Pager triggered for elevated p95 for model-builder-7 (g4dn-like); throughput drop ~15-20%.
- 2026-02-19 07:05 UTC: Rolled FF to 50% by customer tier; partial mitigation but still present.
- 2026-02-20 14:30 UTC: Started deeper debug (this doc).

Commands run / data collected:
- Check worker metrics (k8s exec):
  kubectl -n serving-runtime top pod model-7-worker-0 --containers
  -> CPU ~14%, MEM ~32Gi, GPU util ~42% (was ~70% before).

- Collect runtime logs (grep):
  kubectl logs model-7-worker-0 | grep -E "batch_size|kv-cache|continuous" -n -A2 -B2 > /tmp/model7-batching.log
  Snippet from logs:
    [2026-02-19T06:18:12Z] INFO batching: continuous_batching enabled=true max_batch_tokens=4096
    [2026-02-19T06:18:12Z] DEBUG batching: created 1 batch(es) from 7 queued reqs (avg_len=1392, max_len=2048)
    [2026-02-19T06:18:12Z] WARN batching: dropping prefix cache for req=abc123 (kv_cache_miss=true)

- Reproduced locally with loadgen (seq dist skewed to >1024):
  ./loadgen --qps 80 --model rdx-large --seq-dist heavy_long --enable-continuous=true --concurrency 12
  Observed: throughput 1.2k tokens/s, p95 latency 980ms.
  With --enable-continuous=false: throughput 1.45k tokens/s, p95 760ms.

- Checked batching histograms (prometheus query):
  sum by (batch_size) (rate(serving_batch_created[5m]))
  -> spikes at batch_size=1 and batch_size=8; fewer mid-sized batches (16-64) than expected.

Error / warning snippets seen:
- WARN batching: short-circuit flush due to stop_condition met (queued_time_ms>150ms)
- ERROR kv_cache: mismatch detected: key_count=0 expected>=1 (this happens on 12% of long requests)
- DEBUG routing: fallback to model-variant-2 due to kernel-mismatch: quantized->fp16

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) Continuous batching heuristics rely on sequence-length histogram to form batches; the recent change to treat streaming partials as "not-yet-ready" may delay coalescing and cause more small batches for long sequences. Leads to lower GPU occupancy.
2) KV cache invalidation: for long sequences the KV cache hit-rate dropped due to prefix trimming (we observed "dropping prefix cache" log). This increases compute per token and reduces throughput. Possibly correlated with new prefix-eviction threshold introduced in PR GH-PR#328.
3) Kernel selection path: fallback to FP16 kernels for certain long sequences causing slower execution (seen in routing debug). Could be model variant compatibility issue after auto-quantization policy changed.
4) Autoscaler + batch accumulation: with continuous batching enabled, accumulation targets are lower which interacts poorly with our autoscaler pod replica targets causing underprovisioning at certain qps patterns.

Quick checks attempted (results):
- Toggle continuous batching on a single worker (staging): set env CONT_BATCHING=off, restart pod -> local loadgen numbers improve ~20%. Suggests CB is involved.
- Reverted PR GH-PR#328 in canary: telemetry shows kv_cache_hit_rate back to ~88% (from 72%), throughput recovers ~12%.
- Increased batch_max_wait_ms from 15 -> 50 in staging config: more coalescing, throughput improved but p50 latency slightly worse.
- Forced kernel pin to fp16 for model variant in canary: throughput improved marginally; suggests kernel fallback part of problem but not primary driver.

Metrics / numbers captured:
- Before change (baseline): throughput ~1.6k tokens/s, GPU util ~70%, kv_cache_hit_rate 0.89, p95 720ms
- After change: throughput ~1.3k tokens/s, GPU util ~42-48%, kv_cache_hit_rate 0.72, p95 980ms
- Local repro (heavy_long): CB=true -> 1.2k tokens/s, CB=false -> 1.45k tokens/s

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- Roll back PR GH-PR#328 from canary to 0% and monitor kv_cache_hit_rate + throughput over 2h. (Owner: Priya)
- Add verbose KV cache logs for a 10-minute window on affected workers to capture why key_count=0 occurs (Owner: Maya).
- Instrument sequence-length histogram at routing layer (already added a gauge; need to collect for 24h). (Owner: Ethan)
- Run controlled experiment toggling batch_max_wait_ms across [15,25,50,100] and measure tokens/s vs p95 for long-seq load. (Owner: Ethan)
- Add guard in continuous-batching to avoid treating streaming partials as "not-yet-ready" unless they are <X tokens. Quick patch: treat partials with >512 tokens as ready for coalescing. (Draft PR idea). (Owner: Liam)

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Revisit the interaction matrix between continuous batching heuristics, autoscaler settings, and model quantization/variant selection. Create a couple of unit/integration tests that simulate heavy-long workloads.
- Add synthetic telemetry that can be toggled per-customer to simulate sequence-length skews during CI.

Notes / random observations:
- Noticed higher variance in batch composition when upstream traffic has many streaming calls (chat-like) mixed with single-shot long requests; we need smarter separation or tiny per-route policies.
- Customer X (tenant id t-9) saw biggest impact; their seq distribution is 70% >1024. Consider targeted rollback for high-impact tenants until fixes land.
- Some of the logs show TLS chunking delays that might amplify queued_time_ms; network layer still not ruled out fully.

References: GH-PR#328-cc-batching-fix, JIRA-INFR-4821, slack:/channels/#serving-runtime/thread/3F4a9

Short-term conclusion:
Evidence points to continuous-batching heuristic interacting with KV cache eviction policy (PR GH-PR#328) as the dominant cause. Kernel fallback and autoscaler interactions are contributing factors. Priority is to revert the KV cache change in canary, run controlled batch_wait experiments, and add telemetry on seq-length histograms and KV cache events.

-- Ethan
